workplace_or_process: Globe Union lead-acid battery plant, Bennington, Vermont
finding: 35 samples equaled or exceeded 200 µg/m3; 93 equaled or exceeded 100 µg/m3; 172 equaled or exceeded 50 µg/m3. NIOSH concluded that a hazard of exposure to airborne lead existed at this plant.
limitations: This finding applies to the evaluated battery-manufacturing workplace. It does not establish airborne lead concentration, release, exposure, route, dose, or conditions aboard a submarine or for any particular shipmate.

workplace_or_process: Globe Union lead-acid battery plant, Bennington, Vermont
finding: 19 of 143 workers had blood lead concentrations of 60 µg/dL or above; 63 had 40-59 µg/dL. EP values above 100 µg/dL whole blood were found in 56 workers and correlated with blood lead levels.
limitations: These are findings in workers at the evaluated battery-manufacturing plant. They are not biomarker evidence for any shipmate and do not establish submarine exposure or causation.

workplace_or_process: Globe Union lead-acid battery plant, Bennington, Vermont
finding: No antimony concentrations exceeded the OSHA or NIOSH recommended standard; salvage and remelt workers had the highest measured antimony levels.
limitations: NIOSH documented antimony as a grid material and measured occupational exposure at this battery plant, but did not find concentrations exceeding the cited standards. This does not establish antimony exposure aboard a submarine or for any individual shipmate.

workplace_or_process: Globe Union lead-acid battery plant, Bennington, Vermont
finding: No sulfuric acid concentrations exceeded the OSHA or NIOSH recommended standard. The plant process used sulfuric acid in paste mixing and battery filling.
limitations: This establishes sulfuric-acid use and measured airborne exposure conditions at the evaluated battery plant only. It does not establish sulfuric-acid handling, mist generation, concentration, or individual exposure aboard a submarine.

workplace_or_process: Globe Union lead-acid battery plant, Bennington, Vermont
finding: Stibine was measured during the evaluation; no stibine concentration exceeded the OSHA standard and no combined arsine/stibine exposure exceeded recognized health standards.
limitations: This is battery-industry comparison evidence only. It must not be used to infer that stibine was generated aboard a submarine. Evidence of the relevant shipboard materials, chemistry, charging conditions, generation, and exposure would be required independently.
